notes: Existing vp_nahusha is reused as Āyus’s son; this batch does not create a duplicate Nahuṣa node. Every other node is source- and branch-scoped to avoid merging common names with similarly named figures elsewhere in the graph.

Count: 41 new named-person nodes plus the existing Nahuṣa anchor = 42 named individuals. One additional unnamed king of Kāśī is represented as an unnamed individual so the explicit Kāśya → king of Kāśī → Dīrghatamas sequence remains intact; that intermediary is not included in the named-person count.

Pratardana, Śatrujit, Vatsa, Ṛtadhvaja and Kuvalayāśva are represented as one person because the passage explicitly equates those names. The chapter-8 digital Sanskrit text has different readings (including Suhotra’s sons and the Kāśī genealogy); relationships here follow ANU’s translation.

Raji’s 500 sons are unnamed as individuals and are omitted rather than represented as an anonymous collective. The exchange in which Indra calls Raji a father and himself a son is presented as political flattery; it is not encoded as biological ancestry. Rambha is noted in the source as childless, with no descendant node inferred.

Kṣatravṛddha has two separately attested descendants in this passage: Suhotra in 4.8.2, and Pratikṣatra in 4.9.14. Since neither is described as his only son, both lines are retained without forcing them into a single exclusive succession.
